title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
desc: 時間旅人來到公元802,701年，地面上是悠閒的伊洛伊人，地底下卻藏著莫洛克人。

intro: Let's discuss H. G. Wells's 'The Time Machine.' The Time Traveller visits the year 802,701!
我們來討論威爾斯的《時間機器》。時間旅人造訪了公元802,701年！

q: The Eloi live entirely on fruit. No cattle, no farms, apparently no effort at all. Does a purely fruit-based diet sound utopian or unsettling to you?
伊洛伊人完全靠水果維生。沒有牛群、沒有農場，看起來毫不費力。純水果飲食對你來說聽起來像烏托邦，還是令人不安？
o: Utopian at first, but I'd miss the variety.
一開始像烏托邦，但我會想念多樣性。
variety = 多樣性。at first = 起初。
The Traveller feels the same. Before long, he's craving meat.
時間旅人也有同感。沒多久他就很想吃肉。
Unsettling. Nothing comes for free.
令人不安。天下沒有白吃的午餐。
Nothing comes for free = 沒有東西是免費得來的。
A sharp instinct, and a spoiler of sorts: someone underground is paying the price.
敏銳的直覺，也算某種劇透：地底下有人在付出代價。
Honestly, it sounds like a healthy detox.
老實說，聽起來像健康的排毒餐。
detox = 排毒。
Ha! An 800,000-year juice cleanse.
哈！一場八十萬年的果汁排毒。

q: They dine together in a huge, decaying hall, using slabs of polished stone as tables. How much does the setting matter when you eat?
他們在一座巨大而破敗的大廳裡一起用餐，用磨光的石板當桌子。用餐環境對你有多重要？
o: A lot. A good atmosphere makes food taste better.
很重要。好的氛圍讓食物更美味。
atmosphere = 氣氛、氛圍。
Research supports that. Lighting and music genuinely affect how we taste.
有研究支持這點。燈光和音樂確實會影響我們的味覺。
Not at all. I often eat at my desk.
一點也不。我常在辦公桌前吃。
not at all = 一點也不。
Very modern, and a little bleak, much like the Eloi's ruined hall.
很現代，也有點淒涼，很像伊洛伊人的廢墟大廳。
Company matters more than the room.
同伴比空間更重要。
company 在這裡是「同伴」，不可數。
A lovely point. The Eloi eat together but barely talk: company without conversation.
說得好。伊洛伊人一起吃卻幾乎不交談：有伴卻沒有對話。

q: Wells suggests that when every need is met, humanity loses its drive. Are convenience foods and delivery apps making us less capable?
威爾斯暗示，當所有需求都被滿足，人類就失去了動力。便利食品和外送 app 是否讓我們變得更無能？
o: To some extent. Many people can't cook basic meals anymore.
某種程度上是。很多人已經不會煮基本的餐點了。
to some extent = 某種程度上。not ... anymore = 不再。
That's an Eloi-like drift. Convenience quietly erodes our skills.
那是一種伊洛伊式的漂移。便利悄悄侵蝕我們的技能。
No, it frees up time for other things.
不會，它幫我們騰出時間做別的事。
free up = 騰出（時間、空間）。
A fair counterargument. The Eloi, however, used their free time for nothing at all.
合理的反駁。不過伊洛伊人把空閒時間完全浪費掉了。
It depends on what we do with the saved time.
取決於我們如何使用省下的時間。
It depends on what... = 取決於…什麼。
Precisely the question Wells leaves us with.
這正是威爾斯留給我們的問題。

q: The Traveller strikes matches to scare off the Morlocks, and he's horrified to realize what meat they eat. If you could bring one food back from the future, would you?
時間旅人點燃火柴嚇退莫洛克人，並驚恐地意識到他們吃的是什麼肉。如果你能從未來帶一種食物回來，你會帶嗎？
o: Only if I knew exactly what was in it!
除非我確切知道裡面有什麼！
Only if I knew... 假設語氣：只有在我知道…的情況下。
After the Morlock revelation, that's a very wise condition.
在莫洛克人的真相揭露後，這是很明智的條件。
Yes, lab-grown meat that's actually delicious.
會，真的很好吃的實驗室培育肉。
lab-grown meat = 實驗室培育肉。actually = 真的、確實。
That's a science-fiction idea that's quickly becoming reality.
那是一個正迅速成真的科幻點子。
No, I'd bring back seeds instead.
不，我會改帶種子回來。
instead = 改為、取而代之。
Poetic! Weena gives him two strange white flowers, the only proof of his journey.
好有詩意！薇娜送他兩朵奇怪的白花，那是他旅程唯一的證據。

end: Chilling and brilliant. Next time, let's explore the ruined buildings of the future.
令人發寒又精彩。下次來探索未來的廢墟建築吧。

intro: Let's look at the architecture of the future. Wells paints such haunting ruins.
我們來看看未來的建築。威爾斯描繪的廢墟令人難忘。

q: The Eloi live in vast communal buildings with no private homes at all. Could you give up private space entirely?
伊洛伊人住在巨大的共同建築裡，完全沒有私人住所。你能完全放棄私人空間嗎？
o: Never. Privacy is essential to me.
絕不。隱私對我來說不可或缺。
essential = 不可或缺的。
Wells hints that without privacy, individuality fades too.
威爾斯暗示，沒了隱私，個性也會跟著消失。
Maybe, in a close-knit community.
也許可以，在關係緊密的社群裡。
close-knit = 關係緊密的。
Co-living spaces are testing exactly that idea today.
今天的共居空間正在實驗這個想法。
I did it in a college dorm. Once was enough!
我大學住宿舍時體驗過。一次就夠了！
dorm = dormitory 宿舍。Once was enough = 一次就夠了。
Ha! Dorm life is our closest real-world Eloi simulation.
哈！宿舍生活是現實世界最接近伊洛伊人的模擬。

q: The Morlocks live underground and reach the surface through well-like shafts. Would you ever live in an underground home, like the cave houses in some deserts?
莫洛克人住在地底，透過像井一樣的豎坑到達地面。你會住地下的房子嗎，像某些沙漠地區的洞穴住宅？
o: Yes, with good ventilation and light wells.
會，只要有良好的通風和採光井。
ventilation = 通風。light well = 採光井。
Spoken like an architect! Coober Pedy in Australia is a real example.
像建築師說的話！澳洲的庫伯佩迪就是真實例子。
No, I'd feel claustrophobic.
不會，我會有幽閉恐懼。
claustrophobic = 有幽閉恐懼的。
Understandable, and Wells exploits exactly that fear.
可以理解，而威爾斯正是利用了這種恐懼。
Only on vacation, not permanently.
只在度假時，不是永久。
permanently = 永久地。
A cave hotel in Cappadocia sounds like the perfect compromise.
卡帕多奇亞的洞穴飯店聽起來是完美的折衷。

q: He finds the Palace of Green Porcelain, a crumbling museum full of rotting books. What would you want future generations to find in our buildings?
他發現了綠瓷宮，一座滿是腐爛書籍、正在崩塌的博物館。你希望未來世代在我們的建築裡找到什麼？
o: Libraries. Knowledge should outlast us.
圖書館。知識應該比我們活得更久。
outlast = 比…更持久。
His despair over the rotten books suggests Wells shared that hope.
他對腐爛書籍的絕望，暗示威爾斯也抱持同樣的希望。
Sustainable buildings that still work.
仍能運作的永續建築。
sustainable = 永續的。
A practical legacy. Durability is the ultimate green feature.
實用的遺產。耐久性是終極的環保特性。
Ordinary homes, to show how we really lived.
普通的家，展示我們真正的生活方式。
ordinary = 普通的。
Like Pompeii: everyday kitchens tell us more than palaces do.
就像龐貝：日常的廚房比宮殿告訴我們更多。

q: The novel ends with the Traveller vanishing again, perhaps forever. If you could travel in time, would you rather see the architecture of the past or of the future?
小說以時間旅人再次消失作結，也許永遠不回來。如果你能時空旅行，你想看過去的建築還是未來的建築？
o: The past, especially ancient cities at their peak.
過去，特別是古城在鼎盛時期的樣子。
at their peak = 在巔峰時期。
Imagine Rome with its original painted marble!
想像一下羅馬原本塗著彩色的大理石！
The future. I'm curious about vertical cities.
未來。我對垂直城市很好奇。
vertical = 垂直的。
Skyscraper farms and sky bridges. Hopefully not built over Morlock tunnels!
摩天農場和空中天橋。希望不是蓋在莫洛克人的隧道上！
Neither. I'd visit my grandparents' house when they were young.
都不要。我想去看祖父母年輕時的家。
neither = 兩者都不。
That's the most touching answer. Personal history is its own time machine.
這是最動人的答案。個人的歷史本身就是一台時光機。

end: Thank you for travelling through time with me. Until the next era!
謝謝你陪我穿越時空。下個時代見！
